lessons: Art fills ~85-90% of the canvas height; width follows the object (b22 armchairs 18 wide at size 22). Asking for "narrow" does not narrow it (b28 dressers 24 wide, stoves 20).
Size 16 is below what the batch model draws well (lineless mush): use 20-22 for small items, Pixen 16x16/20x20 (1 generation) for single small sprites.
Sizes above 32 cost 15 per 64-slot batch (b36), not 10.
Pro Flash (5 per image) gives an exact canvas such as 16x32: good for narrow wall-run pieces (bookcase, pantry, stove); busy patterns (patchwork) turn to noise at 16 px wide.
Cream (#fde2b4 and the like) has no Resurrect 64 match and lands on taupe or sage: map it per sprite in fixups.json.
Flame animation: paint seed flames into the empty hearth, animate_image (1 generation, 6 frames), then keep only fire-colored pixels over the dark interior (fire.mjs).
